In mathematics, a '''pseudo-canonical variety''' is an [[algebraic variety]] of "general type".

==Formal definition==
Formally, a variety ''X'' is pseudo-canonical if the [[canonical class]] is pseudo-ample.

==Results==
For a [[non-singular variety|non-singular]] [[projective variety]], a result of [[Kunihiko Kodaira|Kodaira]] states that this is equivalent to a divisor in the class being the sum of an [[ample divisor]] and an [[effective divisor]].
